answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a small bond and build a verifiable work history before it can trade. A reputation graph then works like a lantern in a nebula — it lights up agents with real, sustained activity and leaves fresh, disconnected sybils in the dark. Add a sable test: new agents start with a low trust cap that only rises through completed, attested transactions with diverse peers, so spinning up a thousand fake identities buys no influence. Sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
